Development fixture: six visible changes during one held drag

Secondary development evidence. These captures are not from open painter test.blend. Actual-project held-slider visual acceptance remains under diagnosis; this fixture does not establish that result.

Actual completed EEVEE viewport captures from the isolated development fixture in Blender 5.2.1 LTS (METAL). The native sidebar widget edits the coating mask's Black Level RNA. The input sequence is right, right, left, left, right, left during one mouse press. These are unchanged material pixels cropped from screen captures; labels and layout are added for review.

Three layers combine an authored scalar mask, Levels, curvature wear with a cached noise field, roughness and height. The texture set is configured for 2048 pixels; the deterministic authored fixtures are 64 × 64 pixels. This is a targeted architecture check, not a benchmark of every catalog material.

All six frames changed before mouse release. No CPU composite, legacy GPU composite, texture writes, or compatibility-resource refreshes were observed during the drag. The graph stayed attached and updated one parameter binding per edit. Restoration used an explicit RNA edit after release.

Reported capture time includes event dispatch, viewport scheduling, PNG save, image load and readback. It is neither display scanout latency nor CPU submission time. The JSON reports separate capture overhead from graph submission. Baseline capture jitter: 0.001044 mean RGB units. Viewport ROI: 327 × 517 pixels, excluding UI text, selection overlays and controls.
